programmes.t: Cosmic Vistas: Windows to Other Worlds / Fountain of Creation
programmes.d: See the sun, moon, planets, and galaxies through the eyes of intrepid machines that are blazing a trail across the solar system. A gateway to bold adventures, these cameras are delivering spectacular new cosmic vistas.

programmes.t: Cosmic Vistas: Virtual Universe
programmes.d: Our understanding of the cosmos is limited by the amount of time we have to see it. Fortunately, computer simulations can help us see how galaxies interact over millions of years, and even how dark matter structures the universe.

programmes.t: Cosmic Vistas: Water Worlds
programmes.d: The key ingredient to life in the universe is water. Until recently we thought Earth was the only place in the solar system to have any water at all. Now that probes are peering around nearby worlds we are finding that is just not the case.

programmes.t: Trajectory - Milestones in Space Exploration: Project Gemini Advances, Cassini at Saturn & More About Mars
programmes.d: Project Gemini Advances - NASA refines the techniques needed for rendezvous. Cassini at Saturn - In the Cassini probe's final years of activity, its handlers are asking it to do more complex and risky assignments.

programmes.t: Inside Outer Space: Episode 4: Black Holes
programmes.d: Come with us as we explore and unravel the mysteries of what lies beyond our planet Earth. This is a series packed with space stories and information about our universe covering what we can see.

programmes.t: Inside Outer Space: Episode 8: Extravehicular Activity
programmes.d: Come with us as we explore and unravel the mysteries of what lies beyond our planet Earth. This is a series packed with space stories and information about our universe covering what we can see.

programmes.t: Trajectory - Milestones in Space Exploration: The Beginning of the End, Apollo Gets Complicated & The End of Apollo
programmes.d: The Beginning of the End - After the first Moon landing the Apollo science program was about to start in earnest but people were losing interest. Apollo Gets Complicated - New technology is added that extends the reach of the Apollo program.

programmes.t: Trajectory - Milestones in Space Exploration: Project Gemini, Venus Express, EMU & Deep Space Communication
programmes.d: Project Gemini Commences - Did Gemini give the US a lead in the space race? Venus Express - The last days of ESA's Venus probe. EMU - NASA's Extravehicular Mobility Unit. Deep Space Communications - ESA's worldwide network of giant dishes.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: Flight Status
programmes.d: The next 12 months will see an intense rise in flight tests, demonstration launches and high priority flights. Some are on time others are not. We check the flight status of some of this new hardware and these new capabilities.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: Juno, Cassini and Beyond
programmes.d: The Amazing Cassini spacecraft and its sibling lander, Huygens, have now concluded their scientific studies, bringing back years of data. Now, Juno piercing the cloak of Jupiter and her distant relative New Horizons at the edge of the solar system.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: Living Planet
programmes.d: We have been observing Earth for 40 years now, in the last 20 we have focus with intensity on the planet with new technologies and capabilities, we have accumulated a mass of data that is now revealing a complex and ever changing living planet.

programmes.t: The Apollo Experience: Apollo 17: Part 2
programmes.d: In this episode, hear first hand testimonials and dialogue from the incredible men who walked on the moon. Incredible footage and photos give a unique and beautiful experience of their data collection process and journey home.

programmes.t: Trajectory - Milestones in Space Exploration: Beyond Earth Orbit, IXV Vehicles & Galileo Satellites Lost and Found
programmes.d: Beyond Earth Orbit - The Apollo program takes bold new steps. IXV Re-entry Vehicle - Europe is working to perfect a re-entry vehicle. Galileo Satellites Lost and Found - Navigation satellites go into incorrect orbit.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: Living with Space
programmes.d: Astronauts and Cosmonauts train and study for years to work and live aboard the International Space Station. With this wealth of experience and insight behind them what do they think when they return to Earth?

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: Cosmic Collisions
programmes.d: Space is vast, yet it is full of collisions. Gas and dust electrostatically flock together, and gravity takes over coalescing grains into rocks. Those rocks become boulders, then asteroids colliding again and again, striking planets and each other.

programmes.t: The Truth is in the Stars
programmes.d: Does our society have the capacity to live up to Star Trek's optimistic vision for humanity's future? William Shatner takes us on a journey to find out whether art has imitated life in the years since the world-renowned TV series premiered in 1966.

programmes.t: The Amazing World of Gravity
programmes.d: This film features unexpected historical insights, cutting-edge science and exciting new experiments. From Einstein's Relativity to quantum mechanics, host Jim Al-Khalili explores one of the most extraordinary phenomena in our universe.

programmes.t: Cosmic Vistas: Borderland / Mars: Red Dawn
programmes.d: See the sun, moon, planets, and galaxies through the eyes of intrepid machines that are blazing a trail across the solar system. A gateway to bold adventures, these cameras are delivering spectacular new cosmic vistas.

programmes.t: Cosmic Vistas: Shooting Gallery: Asteroids and Comets / Galactic Visions: Alien Worlds
programmes.d: See the sun, moon, planets, and galaxies through the eyes of intrepid machines that are blazing a trail across the solar system. A gateway to bold adventures, these cameras are delivering spectacular new cosmic vistas.

programmes.t: Trajectory - Milestones in Space Exploration: To The Moon, SpaceX's Dragon and Falcon & GAIA
programmes.d: To the Moon - The Apollo program achieves its major objective. Dragon, Falcon and Spacex - New directions in re-usable spacecraft. Gaia- Mapping our galaxy in unprecedented detail.

programmes.t: Trajectory - Milestones in Space Exploration: Project Mercury Advancement, Camera Tracking & The International Space Station
programmes.d: Project Mercury Advances - America's first manned space program finally puts a man in orbit. Camera Tracking - The array of special cameras that follow a spacecraft at launch. The International Space Station - The building and operation.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: The Dark Side
programmes.d: In terms of the Universe, we know we don't know much, especially when it comes to dark matter and dark energy. Scientists are devoting so much of their time to discovering as much as the possibly can about this mysterious matter.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: The Gas Giants
programmes.d: In the cold, dark expanse of our solar system, beyond the asteroid belt, lie the giant planets. Some can be seen with the naked eye, others have been visited by our camera. What secrets do they hold?

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: Atmosphere
programmes.d: Our atmosphere is an unbelievably complex machine that protects us from the vacuum of space, shelters us from harmful radiation and allows us and the biosphere to breath; we need to learn much more about it so we can better it.

programmes.t: Cosmic Vistas: Superscopes
programmes.d: The human eye can only see visible light, a small spectrum of electromagnetic waves. Today, we have instruments that let us perceive all wavelengths.

programmes.t: Cosmic Vistas: Night Fire
programmes.d: The Northern Lights are more than just beautiful; they tell us about the make up of our planet, our sun, and may even be a signpost for the possibility of life on other planets.

programmes.t: Trajectory - Milestones in Space Exploration: The Space Race, The Hubble, Chasing Comets & Space Debris
programmes.d: Cold War & The Start of the Space Race - Cold War rivalry and the acceleration of space exploration. Servicing Hubble - Preparations for Hubble's final servicing mission. Chasing a Comet - Launch and the difficult path to rendezvous.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: Stars Above
programmes.d: The life cycle of stars reveal to us the past and the future of Earth and ourselves.

programmes.t: The Apollo Experience: Apollo 17: Part 1
programmes.d: Between 1960 and 1972, mankind boldly went where no human had been before. Across 11 manned missions, 24 men flew to the moon and 12 walked upon its surface. This film documents Apollo 17 through the eyes of the astronauts who flew.

programmes.t: Cosmic Vistas: Cosmic Rays
programmes.d: Cosmic rays can tell us much about the universe. They are not simply another form of light, but carriers of information about powerful and unseen processes at work thousands or even millions of light years away.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: Exo Planets
programmes.d: As scientists and astronomers peer more closely and with evermore fidelity at nearby stars, they are discovering countless exo planets. How many Earth-like planets are out there? Could one of them hold life not so different from our own?

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: First Light
programmes.d: The Hubble Telescope is nearing its end, the replacements are ready to go, ready to peer further back in time and space than can be imagined.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: Invasion Mars
programmes.d: For over 50 years we have bombarded Mars with our probes and landers. Spying from orbit to map terrain, finding her strengths and weaknesses. The time nearing for the full scale invasion of the planet, when humans walk on Mars and claim it for their own.

programmes.t: Cosmic Vistas: Gravity
programmes.d: Gravity has long been a force that has intrigued scientists. Now, for the first time scientists are probing to detect gravity waves in space as well as mapping the gravity patterns of the moon.

programmes.t: Cosmic Vistas: The Giant Planets: Lords of Gravity / Outer Limits: Edge of the Solar System
programmes.d: See the sun, moon, planets, and galaxies through the eyes of intrepid machines that are blazing a trail across the solar system. A gateway to bold adventures, these cameras are delivering spectacular new cosmic vistas.

programmes.t: Cosmic Vistas: Seasons of Saturn
programmes.d: Saturn is the second largest planet and has an astonishing 60 moons in its orbit. Thanks to the Cassini mission, it's also one of the most studied and most photographed planets in our neighborhood.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: Return to the Moon
programmes.d: The moon is our closest celestial companion. It lights our night sky and gently tugs at our shores. Few have walked on her surface, but her allure remains strong.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: Space: Getting There
programmes.d: The new surge in space transportation, privately owned companies vying for government contracts and private entrepreneurs looking to build hotels in space.

programmes.t: Trajectory - Milestones in Space Exploration: Project Mercury, The Mars Express & The Soyuz Launch System
programmes.d: Project Mercury Begins - The start of NASA & America's first manned space program. Mars Express - The European Space Agency's Mars Satellite. The Soyuz Launch System - The gradual evolution of Russia's Soyuz launcher.

programmes.t: Trajectory - Milestones in Space Exploration: The Shuttle Program, The Challenger Disaster & Return to Space
programmes.d: The Shuttle Program - The first re-useable spacecraft. The Challenger Disaster - Pressing launch schedules lead to carelessness and the loss of the Challenger. Return to Space - A re-designed shuttle is back in space with a redefined role.

programmes.t: Trajectory - Milestones in Space Exploration: The Apollo Program Begins, Caves & Planck
programmes.d: The Apollo Program Begins - At the very beginning of NASA's moon project things go wrong. Caves - ESA's special training program for astronauts. Planck - Mapping the cosmic microwave background radiation.

programmes.t: Trajectory - Milestones in Space Exploration: Rebuilding Apollo, Orbiting Carbon & Zero Gravity Training
programmes.d: Rebuilding Project Apollo - After the Apollo 1 disaster NASA resumes manned space flight. Orbiting Carbon Observatory 2 - Monitoring the Earth's Co2 levels in unprecedented detail. Zero Gravity Training - Parabolic flights.

programmes.t: Cosmic Vistas: Landsat
programmes.d: Take a look at Landsat 8, the advanced planetary explorer with a 900 million dollar price tag! It is designed to peer across multiple wavelengths to reveal complex and ever-changing details that are undetectable by the human eye.

programmes.t: Cosmic Vistas: Milky Way
programmes.d: This episode traces our view of the Milky Way, from the mythology of ancient sky watchers to the efforts of scientists to map it from the inside out.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: From There to Here
programmes.d: The sky above is studded with stars and countless galaxies. In them, we can read not only our origin, but also our final destination. Technology is on the brink of taking us to places we have only dreamed of.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: The Moons of Olympus
programmes.d: There are many more worlds in our solar system than just the planets. The mysterious moons of the gas giants may hold much more than we ever imagined. Each one is unique, and each one deserves a scrutinous eye.
